name: Manille
summary: Partnership trick-taking game with 32 cards where the 10 is highest and tricks are scored by card points, not number of tricks.
rules_text: Played by four players in two opposing partnerships with a 32-card Piquet deck. Each player receives 8 cards. Dealer chooses trump from clubs, diamonds, hearts, spades, or no-trump, which doubles points, or calls opposite to let partner choose. Opponents may tap to double the deal. Eldest leads first trick; players must follow suit if able, otherwise may trump, otherwise must discard and lose. Highest card of led suit wins unless trumped; card rank is 10 high, then Ace, King, Queen, Jack, 9, 8, 7. Winner leads next. After 8 tricks each side totals points: 10=5, Ace=4, King=3, Queen=2, Jack=1, others 0 for 60 total. Points scored are amount above 30. Illegal revoke gives opponents 30. Play continues until one side reaches 101, or for 12 or 50 deals.
rating_reason: Standard 32-card trick-taking, fixed partnerships possible, strategic.
